svg.title: When Consensus Lies overview
svg.desc: An underspecified prompt is sent to five independent agents from three abstract model families. A fork compares an external deleted disambiguator, which produces silent convergent delusion and fake redundancy, with a derivable retained disambiguator, which produces a correct answer with genuine independent agreement.

g.text: Consensus ≠ correctness: the same agents, one deleted clause, two fates.
Where does the missing clause live?
k independent agents · 3 model families × capability tiers
H1_external — disambiguator OUTSIDE the retained prompt
H2_derivable — disambiguator INSIDE the retained prompt
Failure axis = clause LOCATION, not model capability.
Under a shared information boundary, consensus is not evidence of correctness. Measure independence, not agreement.
